question.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, we will set our result equal to $\frac{3}{2}.$ 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=2$ and $b=k$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{k}{2(2)} \\  & =-\frac{k}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{3}{2},$ so we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{k}{4} & =\frac{3}{2} \\ -2k & =12 \\ k & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
